newsitem.title: UK: Siberian tiger estimate raised, but only 475 exist.
newsitem.headline: Siberian tiger estimate raised, but only 475 exist.

text.p: The number of tigers roaming the forests of Siberia is almost double previous estimates but there are still only a maximum of 475 animals in the wild, the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) said on Thursday.

Russian and U.S. scientists studied tiger tracks in the far east of Russia during the 1995/96 winter and estimated there were between 415 and 475 Siberian tigers, including around 100 young. WWF commissioned the survey.
"This is very encouraging news but we clearly cannot let up our vital anti-poaching work," the WWF said in a statement. Since 1991 at least 180 tigers have been poached.
The last major survey in 1985 identified only 240 to 250 animals. Calculation of numbers of the mostly nocturnal tiger is difficult, particularly in bad weather.
"WWF's work on anti-poaching is now really beginning to make an impact. If we can maintain this effort, I am much more optimistic about the future," said Robin Pellew, director of WWF-UK said.
The Siberian tiger is the largest of the five surviving tiger species. In addition to the Russian population, a few still survive in Manchuria, China.
